sentences.text: Yamaceratops was a small dinosaur estimated to be 50 cm long and weigh around 2 kg.
A juvenile specimen was estimated to be about three years old and weigh 1.2 kg.
A fossilized embryo found in an ornithischian eggshell was initially referred to Yamaceratops in 2008 but was reidentified as a bird embryo in 2015.
The genus Yamaceratops was described by P. J. Makovicky and M. A. Norell in September 2006.
Fossils of Yamaceratops have been found in the Javkhlant Formation.
Yamaceratops had a wide, thick skull ending in a parrot-like beak used to cut ferns, cycads, and conifers, which it then chewed with posterior teeth.
Examination of Yamaceratops fossils suggests its frill was not used for display and hints at a complex evolutionary history for ceratopsian frills.
Yamaceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Mongolia.
Yamaceratops lived from the Santonian to the Campanian stages, between 85.7 and 72.2 million years ago.
